bullet_points: Article in Atlantic claims The Blue Fighter was artificially generated, days after it won Caine prize for African writers  The Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using AI to write a prize-winning short story after an article in the Atlantic said software had flagged it as almost completely AI-generated.
Kundizeza’s story  The Blue Fighter  was announced as the winner of the prestigious Caine prize for African writers on 6 October.
Five days later, The Atlantic published an  article  by the author and journalist Vauhini Vara titled: “Yet Another Literary prize winner Seems to Be AI.”   Continue reading...

stories.title: Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns
bullet_points: Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr   Guinea-Bissau  has not approved the controversial  hepatitis B  study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday.

The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist.

The Canada-born singer-songwriter, 82, posted footage of her citizenship ceremony on her Instagram account, along with a photo of her next to an American flag, accompanied by the caption: “A journey that began 62 years ago.”  It means that Mitchell can now vote in US elections, something that she had complained she wasn’t able to do.

stories.title: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
bullet_points: At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports  Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a  new report .

More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February,  according to HIV Justice Network , an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report.
Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.

stories.title: Brazil cuts work week to 40 hours in win for Lula ahead of runoff
bullet_points: Congress approves constitutional amendment that bans six-day workweeks, which could affect up to 30 million  Brazil’s congress has approved a constitutional amendment to shorten the working week to a maximum of 40 hours, a move that could affect 30 million workers and that will hand a political victory to the leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ahead of the  presidential runoff  in under two weeks.

In an attempt to overturn the  first-round lead  secured by his opponent, far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula has strongly championed the amendment, which will give some workers an extra day off each week.
